reviewer: blind independent agent source review (second run)

method.input: 15-claim subset of rule_precision_sample.json, selected in committed order: first six D001, first six B006, all three I001
method.source_sha256_verification: All 15 supplied file SHA256 values matched before labeling and before writing.
method.blindness: Read only supplied claims and source files; did not read first-rater labels, reports or review findings.
method.review: Inspected source neighborhoods, compared D001 function-body ASTs excluding signatures, and searched I001 bindings throughout their source files. Applied supplied D001/B006/I001 criteria.
method.limitations: Static source review of 15 supplied claims only; no runtime execution, precision extrapolation, repository edits, git operations, or independent commit identity verification. Pinned source identity taken from input; claimed file contents verified by SHA256.

labels.reason: celery/app/utils.py:223,227 have identical executable return convert(key, key) bodies. Different default mapping bindings change semantics but do not change the syntactic bodies; neither is a no-op.
t/unit/app/test_beat.py:195-196,207-208 define task fixtures whose entire bodies are pass. These are trivial no-op bodies excluded by the criterion.

celery/apps/multi.py:476,479 contain the identical return self._stop_nodes(retry=retry, on_down=callback, sig=sig) body. Different retry defaults are outside the bodies; both perform a substantive stop operation.

t/unit/tasks/test_stamping.py:788,1015 return the same nonempty dictionary {"on_errback": True}. This produces stamping metadata used by the visitor; it is an identical executable body, not a pass/no-op hook.
celery/app/trace.py:207,210 both call self._log_error(task, req, ExceptionInfo()). These identical bodies perform error logging rather than no-op hooks.
t/unit/tasks/test_trace.py:138,954 both execute return x + y. These are identical executable arithmetic bodies, despite being separate test-local task definitions.

celery/backends/rpc.py:88-93 catches cancellation exceptions and only logs at debug level. The earlier warning reports connection loss, not this subsequently caught cancellation failure; there is no checked error channel for the caught exception.
t/unit/worker/test_request.py:105-109 intentionally raises Exception("foo"), captures it, constructs Retry with it, and asserts ret.exc == exc. The caught exception is explicitly checked by the test.

celery/backends/database/__init__.py:233-241 catches any error decoding or applying stamp metadata and executes pass, then returns ordinary decoded metadata without reporting or propagating the caught error.

t/integration/test_redis_backend.py:99-101 appends the caught exception to errors and stops draining; after thread joins, line 120 asserts not errors. This is a checked error channel that fails the test on a captured exception.

celery/backends/database/models.py:85-88 catches errors accessing self.stamps and substitutes stamps = None. The returned dictionary includes this computed default but no checked error signal or reporting.
t/unit/backends/test_base.py:2025-2030 checks the caught exception equals expected_exc and checks no retry sleep occurred. Expected exception propagation is explicitly asserted.

celery/fixups/django.py imports WorkController at line 18 and uses it in the quoted type annotation Optional["WorkController"] at line 132. Quoted type annotations count as binding uses under the supplied criterion.

t/unit/backends/test_couchbase.py imports couchbase at line 15, but never loads that binding. Its fallback assignment is not a use; pytest.importorskip("couchbase") and patch("couchbase.cluster.Cluster") contain ordinary strings, not binding references.
celery/backends/arangodb.py imports AQLQueryError at line 16, but the source never loads that binding or uses it in a type annotation. Line 18 only assigns a fallback None value.
